question: When public statements report that about 97% of scientists agree humans cause climate change, do the primary studies commonly associated with that figure - Cook et al 2013 abstract ratings, Doran and Zimmerman 2009's survey of scientists, and the Cook et al 2016 synthesis - measure the same population and quantity?

results.interpretation: Directly answering both dimensions of the question. Population/frame: the audited frames are distinct - Cook 2013 position-taking abstracts, Cook 2013 authors who self-rated papers, and Doran surveyed specialists (with the 82% broader result retained). Measured quantity: they measure distinct quantities - abstract-text endorsement, author self-rating of a paper's position, and survey answers on whether human activity is a significant contributing factor. Cook 2016 additionally reports a 90-100% range across six studies it describes as independent (a synthesis with overlapping authorship), not reduced to a single figure here.
results.proposition: Cook et al 2016 restate that 4014 of the 11 944 Cook-2013 abstracts (33.6%) took a position, and report a 90-100% consensus range across six studies they describe as independent; the three frames audited here - Cook 2013 position-taking abstracts, Cook 2013 self-rated papers, and Doran's specialist subset - are different populations, not one.

scope.comparison_target: Whether the primary studies associated with the public 'about 97%' figure measure the same population and quantity.
scope.excluded: The truth of anthropogenic warming itself, sources not retrieved (e.g. the Tol 2014 Energy Policy re-analysis), and public statements other than the NASA carrier.
scope.included: Five public primary sources - the NASA consensus carrier, Cook et al 2013, Doran & Zimmerman 2009, Cook et al 2016, and Tol 2016 - and the exact figures, methods, and populations they report.

search_notes: Prior art: PR #76 through PR #81 are preserved needs-evidence receipts for earlier versions of this audit; this successor closes their review gaps. None of the accepted dossiers concern the climate-consensus statistic.
